If you own the fd you can close it straight after the `mmap()` call:

       The mmap() function shall add an extra reference to the file
       associated with the file descriptor fildes which is not removed by
       a subsequent close() on that file descriptor. This reference shall
       be removed when there are no more mappings to the file.

https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/mmap.3p.html

If it's not owned and you aren't `dup()`ing to take a reference it then you don't want to close it either, so this path can be eliminated.

Done, the implementation already follows this approach. The path-based constructor closes the fd immediately after mmap(), and the fd-based constructor does not close it since ownership stays with the caller.
